subject: Order form: invoicing cadence & tax responsibility

Cc: Aurora Health Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: invoicing cadence & tax responsibility

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has reviewed the draft order form and has two sticking points before they can issue a PO:

1) Invoicing cadence: Aurora prefers staggered / milestone invoicing rather than a single advance invoice for the yearly commit. Their suggested split is 30% upfront, 30% at month 4, 40% at month 7. Can Redwood support that while keeping committed spend tracking?

2) Taxes & withholding: we need clarity on which party is responsible for VAT/GST/withholding in each region. For audit they also want a copy of Redwood's tax residency certificate.

Procurement is also asking whether you can accept net45 terms (their standard) instead of net30. If net45 is possible, they will sign faster — otherwise they'll escalate.

I can share the Aurora PO template if that helps.

Appreciate a quick confirmation on these three points so I can move it to legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Vendor Programs
Aurora Health

Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence & tax responsibility

Lydia —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes on staggered invoicing, and we can work with net45. We do need to align on how credits apply against the committed spend if invoices are split — Redwood can support the 30/30/40 split and will track cumulative committed consumption so autorebates/credits apply pro rata.

On taxes: Redwood's standard is to invoice gross and let customers handle local taxes/withholding, but we can add language to allocate VAT responsibility by region for enterprise customers. We'll provide our tax residency certificate as requested (attaching the cert and our proposed redlines for the order form).

I've looped in Marissa from Legal and Karthik in Finance — they'll confirm the exact wording for the order form and any interest/late-payment language.

Next steps:
- I'll upload a redlined order form (attached) with proposed invoicing schedule language and a clause for tax allocation.
- If Aurora can send a signed PO referencing the order form and deal id, finance can accept a PO + DocuSign signature.

Attaching: Redwood_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx, TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf

Best,

Connor / Lydia —

Read through the redlines quickly and adding high-level legal comments:
- Invoicing schedule: Redwood can accept the 30/30/40 split. We should add "aggregate committed amount" language so that credits and true-ups are computed against the total annual commitment. Example clause: "Invoices issued according to the schedule shall be applied against Customer's aggregate annual commitment; unused amounts will be credited/true-downed at the end of the commitment period per Section X."

- Net terms: we can accept net45. Finance suggests adding a non-punitive late-remittance remedy — for example, a flat late fee after 60 days rather than compounding interest. Karhiik, please confirm acceptable fee language.

- Tax allocation: propose a simple allocation table in the order form: Aurora (Customer) is responsible for local VAT/GST and withholding taxes; Redwood will invoice gross and provide the necessary residency documentation. If Aurora requires Redwood to gross-up amounts for withholding, that needs explicit approval and may require a separate provision in the order form (and approval by RevOps).

- PO acceptance: Redwood accepts a PO that references the signed order form and DocuSign signature; include HubSpot deal id on the PO to speed processing.

I'll prepare clean language for the above and send a sanitized redline by Monday.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence & tax responsibility

Connor / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few procurement clarifications from our side:

1) Interest/late fees: Procurement will not accept percentage interest. They will consider a fixed administrative fee for late payments but prefer no punitive charges. If Redwood insists on any late remedy, it should be a nominal flat fee and not accrue.

2) VAT allocation table: Procurement wants explicit language that Redwood will provide VAT invoices with tax amounts broken out by jurisdiction. Also, if Aurora is required to withhold, they will request tax residency documentation before remitting.

3) PO flow: Aurora will issue a PO referencing the order form and HubSpot deal id as long as the redline reflects the 30/30/40 invoice schedule and net45 terms. Procurement needs the final redline to complete legal review this week.

We can accept a flat administrative late fee (e.g., $100 per overdue invoice) instead of interest. Can you confirm Redwood will accept that?

Thanks,
Lydia
